```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Fratoni_2023_funobactam_mouse"))
```

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dkad242>

`r mod$description`

Full citation: `r mod$reference`

The paper is a pharmacodynamic study of the beta-lactamase inhibitor
funobactam given with a human-simulated imipenem regimen. Its only fitted
time-course model is the one-compartment murine plasma PK model packaged here;
every exposure index the paper analyses (`fAUC0-24`, `fCmax`, `%fT>MIC`,
`%fT>CT`) was simulated from that model.

# Population

Specific-pathogen-free female ICR mice weighing 20-22 g were rendered
neutropenic with cyclophosphamide (150 mg/kg four days and 100 mg/kg one day
before inoculation), given uranyl nitrate 5 mg/kg three days before inoculation
to reduce renal clearance, and inoculated intramuscularly in one thigh with
0.1 mL of a ~10^7 cfu/mL suspension two hours before treatment (Methods,
"Animals" and "Neutropenic murine thigh infection model"). For the PK study,
funobactam 1, 10 or 20 mg/kg was given subcutaneously together with the
imipenem human-simulated regimen to 36 infected mice per dose (108 in total),
sacrificed in groups of six at predefined times for cardiac-puncture plasma
(Methods, "Funobactam single-dose studies"). Total funobactam was assayed by
LC-MS/MS and the mean profiles were fitted in Phoenix WinNonlin 8.1.

```{r population}
str(mod$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` (ka) | 7.21 1/h | Results, "PK studies": "first-order absorption rate constant, 7.21 h-1" |
| `lvc` (V/F) | 0.462 L/kg | Results, "PK studies" prints 4.62 L/kg; 0.462 L/kg reproduces Table S1 and Table 2 (see Errata) |
| `lkel` (kel) | 0.41 1/h | Results, "PK studies": "overall elimination rate constant, 0.41 h-1" |
| `fu` | 0.9647 | Results, "Ex vivo plasma protein-binding": overall average binding 3.53%; 1 - 0.0353 |
| `propSd` | fixed(0) | not reported (see Errata) |
| `d/dt(depot)`, `d/dt(central)` | n/a | Results, "PK studies": "PK was best described using a one-compartment model"; subcutaneous dosing with first-order absorption |
| `Cu <- fu * Cc` | n/a | Methods, "Human-simulated exposure PK studies" and Table 2 / Table S1: all indices use free plasma concentrations |

# Virtual cohort

The model has no between-subject variability: each dose level was a single
naive-pooled mean profile from destructively sampled mice. The replication is
therefore deterministic, with one simulated mouse per regimen. There are no
etas, so neither `zeroRe()` nor `omega = NA` is needed (and `omega = NA` would
error on a model with no random effects).

```{r regimens}
# Supplementary Table S1 (dose fractionation) and Table 2 (dose ranging).
# Published free exposures over the first 24 h of dosing.
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,          ~dose, ~tau, ~study,             ~auclast, ~cmax,
  "0.9 mg/kg q6h",     0.9,   6,    "Table S1",          17.8,     1.7,
  "1.8 mg/kg q12h",    1.8,   12,   "Table S1",          18.2,     3.2,
  "3.6 mg/kg q24h",    3.6,   24,   "Table S1",          18.3,     6.3,
  "1.2 mg/kg q4h",     1.2,   4,    "Table S1",          35.0,     2.6,
  "1.8 mg/kg q6h",     1.8,   6,    "Table S1",          35.7,     3.5,
  "3.6 mg/kg q12h",    3.6,   12,   "Table S1",          36.4,     6.4,
  "7.2 mg/kg q24h",    7.2,   24,   "Table S1",          36.6,     12.6,
  "3.6 mg/kg q6h",     3.6,   6,    "Table 2 (interp.)", 71.36,    6.95,
  "7.2 mg/kg q6h",     7.2,   6,    "Table 2 (obs.)",    142.71,   13.90,
  "14.4 mg/kg q6h",    14.4,  6,    "Table 2 (obs.)",    363.70,   36.15
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(regimens$treatment))

make_events <- function(dose, tau, id, treatment) {
  addl <- 24 / tau - 1
  # A once-daily regimen is a single dose within the 24 h window; rxode2
  # resets a non-zero `ii` with `addl = 0` and warns, so pass `ii = 0` there.
  ii <- if (addl > 0) tau else 0
  rxode2::et(amt = dose, ii = ii, addl = addl, cmt = "depot") |>
    rxode2::et(seq(0, 24, by = 0.01), cmt = "central") |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = id, treatment = treatment)
}
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  make_events(regimens$dose[i], regimens$tau[i], i, regimens$treatment[i])
}))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = "treatment",
                       returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(all(c("Cc", "Cu") %in% names(sim)), nrow(sim) > 0)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 1: free plasma concentration over the first dosing interval

Figure 1 overlays the free funobactam profile of each dose-ranging regimen
(0.9, 1.8, 3.6, 7.2 and 14.4 mg/kg q6h) over one 6 h interval. The lines below
are the packaged typical-value model; the paper's 14.4 mg/kg line was drawn
from that dose's own confirmatory PK study, which ran about 25% above dose
proportionality (see the NCA comparison below).

```{r figure1}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("q6h$", treatment), time <= 6) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = factor(
    treatment,
    levels = c("14.4 mg/kg q6h", "7.2 mg/kg q6h", "3.6 mg/kg q6h",
               "1.8 mg/kg q6h", "0.9 mg/kg q6h")
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cu, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.01, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Free plasma funobactam (mg/L)", colour = "Regimen",
       title = "Replicates Figure 1 of Fratoni 2023",
       caption = "Typical-value model; observed means are not reproduced.") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Supplementary Table S1: %fT>MIC of the dose-fractionation regimens

Table S1 was generated by the authors by simulating each dose-fractionation
regimen "using parameters from single dose PK studies", so it is a direct
check of the packaged parameters. `%fT>MIC` is the percentage of the first
24 h with free concentration above each MIC.

```{r ft-mic}
mics <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8)
published_ft <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,       ~`0.25`, ~`0.5`, ~`1`, ~`2`, ~`4`, ~`8`,
  "0.9 mg/kg q6h",  86,      57,     29,   0,    0,    0,
  "1.8 mg/kg q12h", 56,      42,     28,   13,   0,    0,
  "3.6 mg/kg q24h", 35,      28,     21,   14,   6,    0,
  "1.2 mg/kg q4h",  100,     100,    69,   24,   0,    0,
  "1.8 mg/kg q6h",  100,     86,     57,   29,   6,    0,
  "3.6 mg/kg q12h", 70,      56,     42,   28,   13,   0,
  "7.2 mg/kg q24h", 42,      35,     28,   21,   14,   6
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-treatment, names_to = "MIC", values_to = "published") |>
  dplyr::mutate(MIC = as.numeric(MIC))

sim_ft <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time < 24) |>
  tidyr::crossing(MIC = mics) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, MIC) |>
  dplyr::summarise(simulated = 100 * mean(Cu > MIC), .groups = "drop")

ft_cmp <- published_ft |>
  dplyr::inner_join(sim_ft, by = c("treatment", "MIC"))
stopifnot(nrow(ft_cmp) == nrow(published_ft))

ft_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(simulated = round(simulated, 1),
                diff = round(simulated - published, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = treatment, "MIC (mg/L)" = MIC,
                "Published %fT>MIC" = published,
                "Simulated %fT>MIC" = simulated,
                "Difference (points)" = diff) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Supplementary Table S1 %fT>MIC replication.")

# Same parameters on both sides: the only difference is the authors' rounding
# and time grid, so a tight bound is appropriate. The 1.8 mg/kg q6h cell at
# MIC 4 is excluded: Table S1 prints 6%, but the same row's fCmax is 3.5 mg/L
# (below 4) and Table 2 prints 0% for the identical regimen.
slip <- ft_cmp$treatment == "1.8 mg/kg q6h" & ft_cmp$MIC == 4
stopifnot(sum(slip) == 1, ft_cmp$simulated[slip] == 0)
stopifnot(max(abs(ft_cmp$simulated[!slip] - ft_cmp$published[!slip])) < 2.5)
```

41 of the 42 cells agree within 1.3 percentage points. The remaining cell,
1.8 mg/kg q6h at an MIC of 4 mg/L, is printed as 6% in Table S1. That is
inconsistent with the paper itself: the row's own `fCmax` is 3.5 mg/L, so the
free concentration never reaches 4 mg/L, and Table 2 gives 0% for the same
regimen at the same MIC. The simulated 0% agrees with Table 2.

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cu)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cu, treatment)
# Guarantee a time-zero row (pre-dose free concentration is zero).
nca_conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nca_conc,
  nca_conc |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cu = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

nca_dose <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  data.frame(id = i, treatment = regimens$treatment[i],
             amt = regimens$dose[i],
             time = seq(0, 24 - regimens$tau[i], by = regimens$tau[i]))
}))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cu ~ time | treatment + id,
                             concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
                             doseu = "mg/kg")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj,
                                          intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Table S1 rows and the Table 2 row marked "interp." were computed by the authors
from the single-dose model; the Table 2 rows marked "obs." are from separate
confirmatory PK studies at those doses.

```{r nca-compare}
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = regimens |> dplyr::select(treatment, auclast, cmax),
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L", cmax = "mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = paste(
  "Simulated vs published free funobactam fAUC0-24 and fCmax.",
  "* differs by >20%."
))
attr(cmp, "footnote")

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    regimens |> dplyr::select(treatment, study, pub_auc = auclast,
                              pub_cmax = cmax),
    by = "treatment"
  )
stopifnot(nrow(nca_wide) == nrow(regimens))

# Model-derived rows (Table S1 and the interpolated Table 2 row) must match to
# the authors' rounding.
model_rows <- nca_wide |> dplyr::filter(study != "Table 2 (obs.)")
stopifnot(
  max(abs(model_rows$auclast / model_rows$pub_auc - 1)) < 0.02,
  max(abs(model_rows$cmax - model_rows$pub_cmax)) < 0.06
)
```

All model-derived rows agree with the published values to their printed
rounding. The 7.2 mg/kg q6h confirmatory study also agrees within 1%. The
14.4 mg/kg q6h confirmatory study is about 21-23% above the model. The paper
does not discuss the excess; it used that study's observed exposures directly
rather than the model, so the starred row reflects the confirmatory data and
not the extraction.

## The printed volume

The Results print the apparent volume as 4.62 L/kg. Simulating the same
regimens with that value shows it cannot be what the authors used:

```{r printed-volume}
sim_printed <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = "treatment",
                               params = c(lvc = log(4.62)),
                               returnType = "data.frame")
printed_auc <- sim_printed |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 24) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(auc_printed = sum(diff(time) *
    (head(Cu, -1) + tail(Cu, -1)) / 2), .groups = "drop")

nca_wide |>
  dplyr::inner_join(printed_auc, by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::filter(study == "Table S1") |>
  dplyr::transmute(treatment, pub_auc,
                   auc_0462 = round(auclast, 2),
                   auc_462 = round(auc_printed, 2)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = treatment,
                "Table S1 fAUC0-24" = pub_auc,
                "Simulated, V/F = 0.462 L/kg" = auc_0462,
                "Simulated, V/F = 4.62 L/kg" = auc_462) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Table S1 fAUC0-24 (mg*h/L) under both readings.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Volume of distribution.** The Results print `V = 4.62 L/kg`. The packaged
  value is 0.462 L/kg. The authors' own simulated exposures (Supplementary
  Table S1, seven regimens, each with `fAUC0-24`, `fCmax` and six `%fT>MIC`
  values), the interpolated Table 2 rows, the 7.2 mg/kg q6h confirmatory
  study and the Figure 1 curves are all reproduced to their rounding with
  0.462 L/kg, and are all ten-fold higher than 4.62 L/kg gives. Since
  `AUC = dose / (V * kel)`, the gap could otherwise only come from `kel`, but a
  ten-fold smaller `kel` would also change the `Cmax` and the `%fT>MIC`
  durations, which 0.462 L/kg reproduces. The printed value is therefore
  treated as a decimal-place slip.
* **Table S1 cell.** Supplementary Table S1 prints `%fT>MIC = 6%` for
  1.8 mg/kg q6h at an MIC of 4 mg/L. The same row's `fCmax` (3.5 mg/L) and
  Table 2 (0% for the identical regimen) both contradict it, so it is
  treated as a typesetting slip and excluded from the numerical check.
* **Free fraction.** `fu = 0.9647` is one minus the overall mean protein
  binding of 3.53%. The authors state binding was low and not
  concentration-dependent over 1-20 mg/kg; `fu` is held fixed.
* **No variability.** The PK study was destructive sampling with six mice per
  time point, fitted to mean profiles, so no between-subject variability exists
  to report. The paper reports no residual error model either; `propSd` is
  `fixed(0)` and the model is suitable for typical-value simulation only.
* **Bioavailability.** Dosing was subcutaneous only, so bioavailability is
  absorbed into the apparent volume `V/F`.
* **Imipenem not modelled.** The imipenem human-simulated regimen was designed
  from murine imipenem PK parameters published earlier by the same group and
  not reported in this paper. The paper shows funobactam did not alter imipenem
  exposure (Figure 2), so the funobactam model stands alone.
* **Exposure-response not extracted.** The paper's sigmoid Emax fits relate a
  24 h summary index (`fAUC/MIC`, `fCmax/MIC`, `%fT>MIC`, `%fT>CT`,
  `(%fT>CT)/MIC`) to the 24 h change in log10 cfu/thigh. They have no time
  course, and the paper reports only the derived stasis / 1-log / 2-log targets
  and `R^2` (Tables 4, 5 and S2), not `E0`, `Emax`, `EC50` or the Hill
  coefficient. The `Cu` output is what a user needs to compute any of these
  indices for a new regimen.
